title: Glycemic effect of post-meal walking vs insulin injection in type 2 diabetes
author: Onnicha Suntornlohanakul
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.72chqaw
materials: Position: fellowship in endocrinology and metabolism
Primary outcome: HbA1c reduction at 6 weeks
Study design: randomized controlled cross-over study
The post meal walking group (Duration: 6 weeks)
Accelerometer (Triaxial accelerometer, Fitbit zip, Fitbit, USA)
Glucose meter (Freestyle Optium H, Abbot, USA)
HbA1c: Turbidimetric inhibition immunoassay (TINIA) by Roche
Plasma glucose: Hexokinase/Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (HK/G6P-DH) by Abbot
chronic lung diseases or heart failure

steps.title: Recruit eligible participants
steps.instruction: Enroll type‑2 diabetic patients aged 35‑70 years who are on at least one oral hypoglycemic drug and basal insulin, have fasting plasma glucose (FPG) <150 mg/dL, HbA1c 7‑9 %, and meet all inclusion criteria while excluding those with uncontrolled hypertension (SBP > 160 mmHg or DBP > 100 mmHg), recent MI or stroke (<3 months), foot problems that impede walking, alcohol >7 drinks/week, caffeine >400 mg/day, shift work, FPG >250 mg/dL consecutively or HbA1c >9 %. Aim for at least 14 participants; recruit 16 to allow for 20 % dropout.

steps.title: Collect baseline demographics
steps.instruction: Record each participant’s age, sex, medical history, current oral hypoglycemic agents, basal insulin type (intermediate‑acting/NPH, Detemir, Glargine or Degludec), weight, and baseline laboratory values (HbA1c, FPG, serum fructosamine, fasting lipid profile).

steps.title: Train participants on devices
steps.instruction: Instruct participants how to use the Freestyle Optium H glucose meter (Abbott, USA) and the Triaxial Fitbit Zip accelerometer (Fitbit, USA), ensuring they can record glucose values and step counts correctly.

steps.title: Provide diabetes education
steps.instruction: Teach participants insulin injection technique, detection and correction of hypoglycemia, self‑monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG), and dietary counseling.

steps.title: Run‑in week 1 monitoring
steps.instruction: During the first week of the 2‑week run‑in, have participants wear the accelerometer all day, record a 1‑day food diary, and perform SMBG six times in one day (before and 2 h after breakfast, lunch, and dinner).

steps.title: Run‑in week 2 walking and review
steps.instruction: In the second week, participants revisit the clinic to review the food diary and glucose‑meter use; they must walk 15‑20 min after at least one meal per day, starting 15‑30 min post‑meal, while continuing to wear the accelerometer and to record a 1‑day food diary and six SMBG measurements for that day.

steps.title: Randomize and collect baseline labs
steps.instruction: At the end of the run‑in, randomize participants by block design into the post‑meal walking group or the basal‑plus group; collect baseline blood tests (HbA1c, FPG, serum fructosamine, fasting lipid profile, post‑prandial plasma glucose (PPPG) and triglycerides (TG) at 1, 2, 3, and 4 h after a standardized mixed meal).

steps.title: Maintain baseline medications
steps.instruction: Continue each participant’s oral hypoglycemic agents and basal insulin at the pre‑study doses throughout the study.

steps.title: Implement post‑meal walking protocol
steps.instruction: Participants assigned to walking must walk 15‑20 min after at least one meal each day, “as fast as possible,” with step counts monitored by the accelerometer.

steps.title: Implement basal‑plus insulin protocol
steps.instruction: Participants assigned to basal‑plus must use rapid‑acting insulin analog glulisine (Sanofi, France) 15 min before the main meal, starting at 4 units per meal or 0.1 U/kg body weight (whichever is appropriate). Adjust the bolus dose via mobile/LINE application over the first 2 weeks to achieve 2‑hour post‑prandial glucose ≤180 mg/dL.

steps.title: Weekly diet and SMBG recording
steps.instruction: Each week, all participants record a 1‑day food diary and perform SMBG six times (before and 2 h after breakfast, lunch, and dinner).

steps.title: Week 3 clinical assessment
steps.instruction: At week 3, participants visit the investigator to review the food diary and SMBG logs and to provide blood samples for fasting plasma glucose and serum fructosamine.

steps.title: Week 6 clinical assessment
steps.instruction: At week 6, participants again visit the investigator to review the food diary and SMBG logs and to provide blood samples for fasting plasma glucose, serum fructosamine, HbA1c, fasting lipid profile, and PPPG and TG measured at 1, 2, 3, and 4 h after the standardized mixed meal.

steps.title: Washout period and crossover labs
steps.instruction: After completing the first intervention, enforce a 2‑week wash‑out during which participants resume their pre‑study behavior; at the end of wash‑out collect the same set of blood tests (FPG, fructosamine, HbA1c, lipid profile, PPPG and TG at 1‑4 h) before crossing over to the opposite intervention.

steps.title: Standardized mixed‑meal test
steps.instruction: In the morning after a 12‑hour fast, give each participant the Isocal drink (256 kcal; 37 % fat, 50 % carbohydrate, 13 % protein) and measure plasma glucose and lipid profile at 0 h and again at 1, 2, 3, and 4 h post‑ingestion.

steps.title: Define hypoglycemia thresholds
steps.instruction: Record glucose alert level 1 as ≤70 mg/dL, clinically significant hypoglycemia level 2 as <54 mg/dL, and severe hypoglycemia level 3 as neurological symptoms requiring assistance.

steps.title: Data entry and statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Enter all collected data into EpiData version 3.1 and perform statistical analysis using Stata software.
